Q: Is it overkill to run a cron job every minute from my server? A:

Using setTimeout() is not reliable because timers are lost if the server restarts and it doesn't scale well with many alerts. A better approach is running a cron job every minute that checks alerts whose nextStepTime has passed and moves them to the next step. For a more scalable production solution, you can use a job queue like BullMQ or Agenda to handle delayed tasks reliably.

Q: Reading with cat: Stop when not receiving data A:

Surprised I couldn't find it mentioned, but on the off chance somebody stumbles on my comment:

While I generally don't like answers which suggest using another program from the one specifically asked about, if there is not some specific feature of cat that is necessary for the use case, the socat command is ideal for this use.

socat features the -t and -T flags, and can easily be set up to pass between STDIN and STDOUT or really anything you could desire, including files, FIFOs, network sockets, etc.

A key advantage over using timeout + cat is that when the timeout is reached, socat will return a success on exit. Whereas timeout will return a failure style exit status, and if --preserve-status is used, cat also returns a failure style exit status when killed by timeout. This could maybe be worked around by sending a specific signal with the --signal= argument if you really need to use timeout for some reason, but about 30 seconds of skimming manpages and kill signals didn't yield any results.

It also has the advantage that you don't need to rely on shell features to do stuff like writing to files (such as when writing a systemd unit).

On the topic of systemd: it has the minor potential benefit of any output showing up in the journal as coming from socat, rather than timeout.

From the socat manpage:


-t<timeout>
              When  one  channel has reached EOF (that is not ignored through option (ignoreoef, the write part
              of the other channel is shut down. Then, socat waits <timeout> [timeval] seconds before terminat‐
              ing. When during the timeout interval the read part of that other channel gives EOF, socat termi‐
              nates without awaiting the timeout. Default is 0.5 seconds, 0 is valid.   This  timeout  is  only
              useful with addresses where write and read part can be closed or shut down independently.


-T<timeout>
              Total inactivity timeout: when socat is already in the transfer loop and nothing has happened for
              <timeout> [timeval] seconds (no data arrived, no interrupt occurred...) then it terminates. Up to
              version  1.8.0.0 "0" meant "infinite"; since version 1.8.0.1 "0" means 0 and values <0 mean infi‐
              nite, default is -1.
              Useful with protocols like UDP that cannot transfer EOF.

As stated, the -t switch times out based on EOF, so in most cases where one would want to "Time out a cat", that wouldn't already be handled by cat's normal behaviour, the -T option (time out when a certain amount of time has passed without new data hitting the pipe) is what you want.

So to "cat" from STDIN to STDOUT, with a 5 second timeout if no new data enters the pipe, you would run the following (-u specifies a one-way communication between the two, and is probably unnecessary, but could theoretically trigger some weird edge-case without it, I'm unsure):

socat -T 5 -u STDIN STDOUT

Q: Drift v2 error AQDD1035E: Class Probability column null — how should payload and feedback datasets be structured in OpenScale? A:

here's details I found that may be able to guide you to resolve this issue. the root cause I see is that Drift v2 requires one explicit float column per class probability. Arrays in a single column are not supported:

Payload CSV required shape

scoring_id,scoring_timestamp,feature_1,feature_2,prediction,prob_No,prob_Yes
abc-001,2024-01-15T10:00:00Z,45,high,No,0.97,0.03
abc-002,2024-01-15T10:01:00Z,32,low,Yes,0.12,0.88

Feedback CSV required shape

feature_1,feature_2,actual_label
45,high,No
32,low,Yes

No probability columns needed here.

The array format does not work

# THIS breaks Drift v2
prediction,probabilities
No,"[0.97, 0.03]"

# This is the correct format
prediction,prob_No,prob_Yes
No,0.97,0.03

Column names must match your subscription config exactly

subscription.update(patch_document=[{
    "op": "replace",
    "path": "/configurations/0/training_statistics/class_probability_fields",
    "value": ["prob_No", "prob_Yes"]  # must match CSV headers character-for-character
}])

Diagnostic before re-uploading

df = pd.read_csv("payload.csv")

print(df[["prob_No", "prob_Yes"]].isnull().sum())       # must be 0
print((df["prob_No"] + df["prob_Yes"]).round(2).unique()) # must be ~[1.0]
print(df.dtypes)                                          # must be float64

Any nulls in the probability columns = AQDD1035E.

Refs:

  • Payload logging CP4D 4.8.x

  • Drift v2 configuration

  • Troubleshooting Watson OpenScale

Note: there's no standalone AQDD error code reference page in the current IBM docs — the old cp-data/4.8?topic=messages-aqdd URL no longer resolves. The troubleshooting page above is the closest active equivalent

Q: Fastlane command not found in Xcode bots post build trigger A:

Follow this steps:

  1. Navigate inside the repo. e.g.cd TemplateProject.
  2. Add fastlane command.(Since xcode server can't find the Fastlane command you need to specify path)
  3. To know the path navigate to your project folder from terminal and execute command:

which fastlane

Result will look as:

/Users/yourcomputername/.fastlane/bin/fastlane beta

Now use this to create a post Script command as attached in the image

This now makes xcode server find your fastlane.

Q: Multiple warning messages "warning: (Internal error: pc 0x7ffff4688dd5 in read in CU, but not in symtab.)" in GDB, V8 debugging A:

I'm not sure if my problem is the same as you. I'm gdb linux kernel-2.6.24 which is built on Debian-4, and the gdb is running in Arch Linux.

⚠️ warning: (Error: pc 0xffffffff8020c480 in address map, but not in symtab.)
⚠️ warning: (Internal error: pc 0xffffffff8020c480 in read in CU, but not in symtab.)

after add --readnow in command line or symbol-file ./vmlinux -readnow in gdb shell, the problem is disappeared. I'm not sure why and how this can fix, but it did. The solution is given by AI.

Q: What is the cause of my error "Expected a 2-dimensional container but got <class 'pandas.core.series.Series'> instead." A:

I encountered the same issue running this code:

import pandas as pd
from sklearn import preprocessing

df.read_csv('dataset.csv')

enc = preprocessing.OneHotEncoder()
enc.fit(df.loc[:, 'Geography'])

It raises the same error. I solved simply converting the Series to a DataFrame:

# ...
enc.fit(pd.DataFrame(df.loc[:, 'Geography']))

In the same vein maybe the problem in your code could be solved modifying the model.fit() argument:

# ...
model.fit(pd.DataFrame(X_train), Y_train)

Other methods are listed in this answer.
